utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, ladies and gentlemen; good morning to the technical booth and the interpreters; good morning to the OTP, the Defence counsel. Good morning, General Krstic. We are now going to continue your testimony. You are continuing under oath. I see that Mr. McCloskey is already ready to proceed. Mr. McCloskey, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, counsel, General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. McCloskey: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could start with Exhibit 609. This is a 15 July interim combat report to Vinko Pandurevic to the Command of the Drina Corps. If you could put the first page of the English on the ELMO, and I'm going to be concentrating on the fifth and sixth paragraphs, the two little ones near the bottom. There we go. That's perfect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, as we discussed -- this document has been discussed before. The first three paragraphs basically discuss the difficult situation posed by the Zvornik Brigade from the column coming up through them and the Tuzla 2nd Corps threatening on the front lines, but what I would like to ask you about is the paragraphs that start "An additional burden." And let me read the phrases and I'll ask you about some things. But to start out with, on 15 July, we know that large numbers of Muslim prisoners have been distributed throughout the schools in the area of the Zvornik Brigade responsibility, at the school in Orahovac, at the new school in Petkovci, at the school in Kula near Pilica, and presumably the school in Rostovici. You've heard the evidence from the survivors and from Mr. Butler. Do you challenge the fact that there were numerous prisoners in those schools on July 15th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learnt of this fact during these proceedings. This document went to the Command of the Drina Corps and not to the forward command post of Krivaca. That was where it was dispatched, the Command of the Drina Corps. And if the Commander of the brigade notes here on the basis of the witnesses who testified, I have no reason to challenge it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the first sentence: "An additional burden for us is large number of prisoners distributed throughout the schools in the brigade area." So that's true?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That has been observed by the Brigade Commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "As well as obligations of security." Now, we know from your own version of events that Ljubo Beara, the Chief of Security for the Main Staff is heading the -- General Mladic's plan to murder all the prisoners. And also according to yourself, he was working hand in glove with Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, the Security Chief for the Drina Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I respond to that question in private session, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Agree or disagree. I think all this information came out as part of the public session. I'm not asking for details, just if he can agree or disagree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Krstic, could you just say yes or no, please, to the question put to you by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then we have a restoration of the terrain. This is the term "asanacija terena", in the B/C/S. Would restoration of the terrain include the burying of the bodies at Orahovac and Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that that was what it meant. The "asanacija", restoration of the terrain in the fighting with the 28th Division, they attacked from the rear the 21st Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, my question is --

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Zvornik Brigade. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The burying of bodies from the death field at Orahovac, would that be considered "asanacija terena" or restoration of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the Commander of the brigade had in mind, but I have answered your question. When you speak of "asanacija terena" or restoration, is where combat activities have taken place. And whether it encompasses what you have said, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Burying bodies after a mass execution can also be restoration of the terrain, can it not?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who was engaged in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, my question is, it's a simple one: Burying the bodies on the field at Orahovac, is that -- could that be referred to as restoration of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Restoration of the terrain after combat activities can imply a collecting up the persons killed on both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the burying of the bodies in Orahovac be considered restoration of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether burying bodies comes under the concept of restoration of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It does in the situation of combat, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When there is combat, then there is the collection, and this is done by the units in charge of restoration and gathering the bodies of those who were killed on either side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what does Vinko Pandurevic mean when he says "the burden for us"? Is he speaking of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he is speaking about the prisoners whom someone brought to the area of responsibility of his brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you what the meaning of "us" is.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Zvornik Brigade probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if the Zvornik Brigade's obligations of security were the obligations imposed on them by Colonel Beara, what would those obligations have been?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably security, security of the facilities and features where the prisoners were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Beara's job was to see to it that thousands of Muslim prisoners were murdered; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered that question earlier on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next paragraph: "This command ..." Does he mean the Zvornik Brigade command?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "This command cannot take care of these problems any longer." Now, "these problems," these are the problems of obligation of security and restoration of the terrain, are they not?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is probably thinking of the security issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one we just spoke of regarding the responsibilities imposed upon him by Ljubo Beara, pursuant to orders from General Mladic? I'm sorry. I interrupted you. What was your answer? You said yes?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't answer the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me try to clear it up. So the problems that Vinko Pandurevic cannot take care of any longer are the obligations of security; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is probably thinking of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, by that sentence, "The command cannot take care of these problems any longer," by that sentence we know that he has been taking care of those problems up until the time he wrote this letter, can we not?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when the prisoners of war started arriving there, what that time period was. On the 14th, between the 14th and 15th of July, he returned from Zepa to his own area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "... as it has neither the material nor other resources. Now, the material needed for the mass execution of hundreds of Muslims are ammunition; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he's thinking about that. I don't think Vinko Pandurevic is thinking of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the material needed for mass executions are ammunition; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, ask the General what material he thinks is necessary for executions, and then you can go into the specificities of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, what materials are needed for executions in the context like Orahovac, when you have those sorts of numbers?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what materials are needed. That is something that the person that did that, executed that, knew, and it wasn't Vinko Pandurevic, and I am quite sure that he wasn't thinking of those materials. If he was thinking of anything, he was probably thinking of food for his brigade and for the prisoners of war. He does not speak here at all about executions of any kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "If no one takes on this responsibility, I will be forced to let them go." Who is he referring to? Letting who go?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Located in the schools distributed throughout his area?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he said: in the schools.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you saying that the burden that he's concerned with is the care and feeding of those prisoners; if someone doesn't take care of the care and feeding of those prisoners, he's going to have to let them go?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those are the prisoners that were blindfolded and murdered on the field of Orahovac, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether at that time when Vinko Pandurevic was writing his report whether the prisoners of war were blindfolded, had blindfolds on their eyes, because he doesn't speak about that in his report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the survivor witnesses who described the dead that piled up in the gym, that died of exposure or something else and were pushed off into a corner of the gym?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember when a witness spoke about that, but Vinko Pandurevic, in his report, makes no mention of that anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit 627.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Can I just ask a couple of questions to straighten something out. Vinko Pandurevic had been with you, General, at the forward command post before he was called back to his brigade down in Zvornik; is that right? He had been up in Zepa with you?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: At the forward command post? Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. He wasn't at the forward command post, he was with his unit in the area of deployment for the completion of the assignment towards Zepa. So he was in that area towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand. So he would have known where you were though. He knew at that time that you were at the command post, would he not, at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So when he went back -- when he was called back to Zvornik to take care of this situation and then when he sent his communique, Exhibit 609, who -- it was addressed to the Drina Corps Command; was that not right? I don't have it in front of me, but I think that's right. Is it addressed to the Drina Corps Command? Who would he have expected was at the Drina Corps Command to receive that communique?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This communique was to be received by the Corps Commander, General Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Was General Zivanovic at the regular command post at that time on July 15th when he sent it?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the Corps Commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I know he was Corps Commander. I'm just asking you whether you know whether on July 15th, when this was sent, he was at the corps command post at Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was at the command post in Vlasenica or whether he was somewhere in the area, in the area of responsibility of the corps and those brigades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right. My last question to you is: Did Pandurevic return to the Zepa front after July 15th? Did he come back to his -- the parts of his unit that were in Zepa after July 15th? Did he return or did he stay down in Zvornik with that part of his brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He stayed in Zvornik. He did not go back to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I see. So when was -- when was the next time after July 15th that you saw or had reason to talk to Pandurevic personally, face to face? Do you remember when you next saw him personally?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember when I next saw him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Do you remember whether it would be weeks or months later or a few days later?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I saw Colonel Pandurevic with his unit in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Krajina Corps in Western Bosnia when I went there to tour the units in that corps and his unit among all the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: And last part of my question: At that time, although that was later, obviously, at that time did you have any discussion or conversation with Colonel Pandurevic about these events?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not talk to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I too have two questions for you. Pandurevic, he left for his area of responsibility, but before that he was with you at the Zepa operation. That was the zone or what was -- what were his tasks, his assignments in the Zepa operation? Could you remind me of that, please?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had his own assignment stemming -- pursuant to the order for Zepa with part of his unit, like all the other units that were engaged for Zepa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And his brigade, where was it deployed? What area?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean towards Zepa? It was deployed in the area of Podplan, which was the area of deployment when the unit arrived in the area, and from there it was to go to accomplish its assignment towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, he had to leave. Did he inform you that he would have to leave?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He received orders. He got orders from me, that is to say, from General Zivanovic, in fact. General Zivanovic called and said that he had to return urgently with his unit, and that was on the 14th of July. I think it was in the afternoon hours, that the situation was highly complex and serious in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade. And I conveyed that to Colonel Pandurevic, and in the course of the night, between the 14th and 15th, he returned to his own area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Complex and difficult for what reasons? When I say "complex and difficult," why? I'm asking whether you know, whether you were informed of the reasons that led to the situation and which led to conclude that the situation was difficult and complex.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, because of the attack of the 2nd Corps of the BH army from the direction of Tuzla towards the area of responsibility of the brigade and because of the attack of the 28th Division from the rear, the flanks of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was there any mention of the existence of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no mention at all of the presence of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please continue, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in charge of the brigade command in the absence of Commander Pandurevic up in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff of that brigade, Major Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who would have been the person that would have briefed Pandurevic on the situation in his brigade when Colonel Pandurevic returned on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He should have been briefed and informed on the situation by his Chief of Staff, Major Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke to Major Obrenovic on the 15th of July, didn't you? You had been very clear that the only time you ever found out anything about anything in the Zvornik area while you were in Zepa was in a communication with that brigade.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After General Zivanovic called the forward command post, Major Obrenovic called as well. I don't remember whether I talked to him or it was Colonel Vicic or Major Jevdjevic who talked to him, but at any rate, it happened in the afternoon hours of the 14th. And the contents of the conversation was similar to what was said by General Zivanovic, that is, that the situation was very difficult and that one part of the Zvornik Brigade should return to its area of responsibility, and Obrenovic said that the order of General Zivanovic was conveyed to Colonel Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on 14 July there was a full briefing of the Drina Corps command, including yourself, on the situation in the Zvornik Brigade area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not me. I was informed by the Corps Commander. I am his subordinate. I was the Chief of Staff. I was informed that the situation was difficult, that one part of the Zvornik Brigade should be returned to its area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a -- the command staff was briefed by Major Obrenovic on the situation in the Zvornik area on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Obrenovic called the forward command post after General Zivanovic, and he said that the situation was difficult and he requested that the brigade commander be returned with one part of his brigade to their area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Major Obrenovic actually called the Krivaca forward command post, where you were working?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Through the Drina Corps command, through the communications centre in Vlasenica, that is, the Drina Corps headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were able to get information either directly from Obrenovic or from whoever he talked to at that point, on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to clarify this issue, if I could. I think it's an important issue. So you were able to get information either directly from Obrenovic or from whoever talked to him at that point on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first received the information from the Corps Commander and his order as to what Vinko Pandurevic should do. After that Dragan Obrenovic, the Chief of Staff of the brigade, called, and he requested that one portion of the brigade be returned, that the situation in the brigade's area of responsibility was difficult. And he was told that Colonel Pandurevic had already been ordered to do that. There was not any other information that was provided from Dragan Obrenovic to either myself or to anyone else at the forward command post at Krivaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time on the 14th did Dragan Obrenovic call the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon hours of that day, in the evening. I don't remember the exact time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't need an exact time, General, but afternoon/evening, is that your best estimate?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was sometime around 1800 hours, just before the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So a full briefing, then, on the events that had been going on on the afternoon of the 14th in the Zvornik Brigade area would include what?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, that was not a full briefing. All that was said was that the situation in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade was difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, my question was: What would a full briefing -- assuming he gave you a full briefing, what would a full briefing have involved?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult to respond to assumptions; however, Major Obrenovic referred to a difficult situation because of the attack of the 2nd Corps from the direction of Tuzla and because of the attack of the 28th Brigade in the rear of the 1st Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I'm sorry to interrupt you. This is not an assumption, what we are talking about here. We are talking about military practice and military rules and regulation. That is to say, when a subordinate is supposed to inform his superior about a certain situation, does he have to tell him everything that has happened in the meantime or not? So that was the essence of the question. So if he has to brief him on the situation, what exactly it is that he is supposed to tell him? So we are talking about the military structure here and the chain of command, rules and regulations. Please, General.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Obrenovic spoke only about the difficulty of the situation in his area of responsibility, that the attacks from the direction of Tuzla and by the 28th Division were very fierce, and he wanted the forces of the brigade to be returned, the forces of the brigade that were engaged in the area of Zepa. That was all he said. That was the request made by Major Obrenovic. He didn't speak about anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but General, if we say that a subordinate officer informs his superior officer -- I'm talking about the chain of command here -- and if he tells him, "I'm in a very difficult and a very complex situation," you, as the Chief of Staff, do you accept this as a piece of information? Don't you ask the reasons why? Don't you want to know what kind of information exactly we are talking about? Because if you say the situation is very difficult and complex, you're merely providing an opinion. The person who has to take certain measures and certain decisions has to know what the situation is in reality and what the reasons are. So what we are talking about is: Did he have to explain that piece of information or was it sufficient for him to say that he was in a difficult and a complex situation?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was by all means enough, the fact that he said that the situation in his area of responsibility was very complex and difficult. He didn't convey to him any other piece of information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You have answered the question. Mr. McCloskey, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Krstic, would a full explanation of the situation in the brigade's zone of responsibility on the afternoon/evening hours of the 14th include the facts that they had to store thousands of prisoners in the schools in their area and they had to spend most of the day executing them and burying them, that particular situation? Shouldn't that have been part of a full briefing by Major Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Major Obrenovic didn't even speak about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we can go to Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I've got one last question. When General Zivanovic asked you to relay the order to Major Pandurevic that he should go back and rejoin the rest of his brigade down in Zvornik, where was General Zivanovic physically located? When he told you to relay that order to Pandurevic, where was he?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was at the Vlasenica command post. This is where he called me from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Right. And that was on the 14th, right?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to get that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the question was previously raised in a private session because it concerns information as to who gave that particular piece of information to General Krstic. So I should like to ask to either move into private session or for the question to be withdrawn, bearing in mind the fact that the broadcast is 30 minutes delayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise. I think Mr. Petrusic is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, I'm sorry, I was waiting for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise. I believe Mr. Petrusic is correct on that point, and it would be more appropriate to go into private session based on our agreements and rulings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. We will move into a private session

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We are in public session. Please continue, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, how many kilometres is it from Vlasenica to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 50 kilometres, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit 627A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is an intercept that the Prosecution has dated as 16 July, at 1111 hours, between Colonel Ljubo Beara and a Cerovic. Can you remind the Court: There is a Cerovic in the Drina Corps staff, in the -- is it -- I'm sorry. What is Cerovic's position? I'm running out of words, thankfully.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant commander for morale, religious, and legal affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does the term "triage" mean to you in a military medical sense?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a military sense, as in any other sense, first of all, I think it comes from medicine, this particular expression, "triage." It has to do with the separation of the sick and the wounded and their further treatment. When it comes to the army, this is something that is also done in peacetime as well. Every day triage has to be done on the soldiers, and after the triage they are sent further on for further treatment or examination, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name Trkulja? Is there a Trkulja in the Drina Corps or the Main Staff that was involved in the events around Zvornik between July 16th and July 18th?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should like to ask for a private session, if possible, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Security reasons again, General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us go into private session, please, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit 630A bis. This again is a 16 July intercept, at 1355 hours, between Zlatar and Palma.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, to direct you down near the bottom, this appears to be someone asking for a -- "Just have him brief me on what's new for Zlatar 1." So that means someone is looking for a briefing for the Drina Corps headquarters or the Drina Corps Commander, or can you tell?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know who the person in question is here. This was an intercept, an intercepted conversation. "Palma" refers to the Zvornik Brigade, and "Zlatar" is the code name for the Drina Corps centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: When this makes a reference to Zlatar 1, do you know if that is for -- a briefing for the Drina Corps centre as a command or is it a specific reference to the commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what this refers to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they made a small corridor so the civilians could pull out. And in fact, on the 16th of July Vinko Pandurevic did make a small corridor so the Muslim civilians, as well as soldiers, could go through to the free territory; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I heard here during the trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first time you ever heard about Vinko Pandurevic letting out the Muslim soldiers and civilians was at this trial?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was the first time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I have one further question. General, would Colonel Pandurevic have had the military authority and structure of the army to make a decision like allowing a corridor so that part of this column, which consisted some of soldiers, some of civilians, could go through, or would he, under military structure then in operation, have had to get somebody's consent for that, to create a small corridor so that civilians and military who had been up to this time, apparently, being both fought and captured and taken prisoner, could now go through? Could he have done that on his own authority or did he have to get someone else's authority to create that corridor?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will answer your question regardless of this document. An approval has to be given by the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS for something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: One quick question on that subject.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Vinko Pandurevic got in a little bit of trouble for doing this without the commander's authority, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This seems to be a convenient time for a break, 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could have Exhibit 620A. This is a 16 July intercept at 1358 hours, between the Zlatar duty officer and the Palma duty officer initially, and then it goes into several names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Krstic, if you could take a look at that. I know you've seen that before. Now, this intercept involves, and I'll start at the third line: "Palma duty officer speaking. 500 litres of D2 for Lieutenant Colonel Popovic." Then it goes down and says, "Hello, is that Basevic? And then somebody finally says, "Yes, it is." Is there a Basevic in the Drina Corps staff, General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several Basevics, quite a few Basevics in the Drina Corps staff. Among others, there was Basevic in the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In the command, what was the Basevic in the command?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basevic was a clerk in the technical service, in the logistics base of the Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would he deal with fuel allocations as part of his job?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether that is his job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this field, in the command staff, you have no idea whether or not he might be involved in getting fuel allocations at times in the Technical Services Branch?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is ensured by the Assistant Commander for Logistics, and from the Technical Service as well that would be to be too, from the Traffic and Communications Service as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On 16 July, there were buses -- by the evidence that has been presented in this case, there were buses travelling from the Kula school in Pilica to the Branjevo farm all day long transporting prisoners to the execution fields at Branjevo farm. And if Lieutenant Colonel Popovic was going to need fuel for those buses, how would he go about getting it if he started running out of fuel?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know at all whether he dealt in fuel, Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, whether he needed fuel at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: If Popovic did need fuel for any job, how would he go about getting it?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would request the Assistant Commander for Logistics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he would do something like in one of the lines down near the bottom: "He just called me from the field and told me to pass you the message over there." So Popovic might call from the field from the Drina Corps and pass the message on that he needed fuel? That would be one day to do it?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. On the second page of the English there's a mention that: "Well, then get in touch with Rosevic." Do you know a Rosevic in the Drina Corps Command Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have any Rosevic in the Drina Corps Command Staff. I don't know that surname at all in connection with the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a place called Rocevic near Kozluk, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the Basevic you're referring to in the technical service a clerk?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't mention any Vasic in the Technical Service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It was Basevic.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the Technical Service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't there, in fact, a Major Basevic, that you used to drive to work with, in the Technical Services?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. That was Lieutenant Colonel Basevic. I don't know whether he was a Major at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his job?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His job was to see to the fact that the technical equipment functioned properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could he be involved in the fuel?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A technical state of weapons. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. On the second page in the English, in the middle, it says, "Give me the operations duty officer. Is Major Golic there by chance?" And then someone answers, "Yes," and then the person says, "Let me talk to him." And then the person says, "Golic, Pop just called me and told me to contact you. 500 litres of D2 to be sent to him immediately, otherwise, his work will stop." Then it talks about a bus loaded with fuel going to Pilica village. Now, we know that Pilica village is the village that the Kula school is located at, don't we?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm afraid we cannot hear the General's answer. The microphone does not seem to switch on for the first one of words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They're not getting your response, so you may need to try to speak into the microphone. It may be a faulty mic. So try to speak up if you could, I think.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I turned my head towards the map. The village of Pilica is on the road towards Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then at the bottom of the page we have Lieutenant Colonel Krsmanovic, who we've learned was -- what was his job again?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Drina Corps we had several Krsmanovics as well, and Krsmanovic was the head of the Traffic Department in the Command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was a Lieutenant Colonel at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was a Lieutenant Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could go to 619A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a material list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the purpose of this document?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of every material list is what has been issued and received with respect to the technical resources and materiel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so the substance of this exhibit indicates that Lieutenant Colonel Popovic received 500 litres of diesel fuel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not compile this document. It says here to whom it is dispatched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that addressee station is for Lieutenant Colonel Popovic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the document that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is the Zvornik Brigade involved in any way in this document?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has the stamp of the Zvornik Brigade, the military post from Zvornik, but whether this is its military post, I don't know. There were other military posts, apart from the Zvornik Brigade military post, in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see any personnel from the Main Staff mentioned in this document?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it, no. I don't know who it refers to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you see any indication in this document that the Main Staff is involved in this transaction in any way?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who these individuals are, the signatures of these individuals, so I can't comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In space 14, under -- is it name and address of recipient, in the original I believe it just -- it says "KDK." And what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: KDK could be an abbreviation for the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is my understanding is the meaning of that, and I note that the translation says "commander of the Drina Corps," and that should be changed and corrected to be "command of the Drina Corps."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Command of the Drina Corps. The interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we'll try to have that straightened out for your exhibits. If we could now go to Exhibit 63A [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, just one moment, please. [In English] I would like to see the document, please. [Interpretation] General Krstic, you have before you, and on the ELMO as well, you're reading the special service organ: "M. Krstic." Could you tell us who that person is?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who that person M. Krstic is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see in the English version, and I haven't got the B/C/S version, but I think that there is a signature, at least in the B/C/S version. Is there in fact a signature? Does a signature exist? And if so, do you know that signature? Do you recognise the signature, General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not. There were a number of Krstics in the logistics base, in Sokolac, for example, in the 35th Base in Bijeljina, and there are people with the surname Krstic on the territory of the Zvornik municipality as well. I don't know whether they had any particular Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but to have diesel fuel, would this document have to go to Sokolac or Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, supplies for all the units in the area came from the logistic base at Sokolac and Bijeljina, and I think that the Zvornik Brigade relied on logistic supplies at the 35th Base in Bijeljina. They relied on that base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Mr. McCloskey, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, Mr. Butler testified about this document, and I believe he identified these names. It is not part of the Prosecution's submission that this M. Krstic is the General. We believe he's a conscript in the Zvornik Brigade. And there's a Milorad Krstic in the logistics branch. There's also, at the bottom right-hand corner, received by Branko Bogicevic. There's also a Zvornik person by that name also. And if we then -- I think we're at Exhibit 635A, and the transcript may have -- may be wrong when I mentioned this before, so we should try to fix that, if possible. It's 635/A. This is a 16 July intercept in the afternoon of 1602 hours, between Zlatar and Palma, and Zlatar says: "Give me 01."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would 01 be, General, in this context?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zlatar 01. I don't know whether anybody had that name, code name. I don't know whether it was the duty officer, operative officer or the Corps Commander, or what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't 01 the Corps Commander?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know that 01 referred to the Corps Commander. That is not stated in any document. It doesn't say in any document that the commander is referred to as 01. He has his name and surname and his rank and duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And extension 385, that's the same extension that in the intercept of 15 July that General Zivanovic referred Colonel Beara to call. Does it help refresh your recollection on the 385 and whose extension that may have been on 16 July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit 638/1A, and if the General could be given the B/C/S version, which is 638/1B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Krstic, while you were in -- operating in Zepa, did you ever need fuel?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Never had to go through Basevic to get some fuel?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no need. The fuel for motor vehicles was not very often used. The vehicles were not often used. And as I have already said in relation to the Srebrenica operation, the units that took part in the operation relied on their logistical support.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit 622A now. This is a 16 July intercept at 2116 hours between Colonel Popovic, who asked to be connected with General Krstic, and Krstic was not there so he asked to be connected with the OC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, I will take this opportunity and tell you that there is a correction that needs to be done on the transcript, as the registrar has just informed me. Madam Registrar, what is it all about? Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's Exhibit 635/A. You said "635/1A," so I just wanted to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mine had "1A" on it, but I think we know which one it is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, if you could take a moment -- have they given you the B/C/S version of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The General needs the B/C/S version of 622A. He can have mine if that will simplify it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, if you could take a moment to familiarise yourself with this intercept which we have again seen before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your question, Mr. McCloskey, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Krstic, this begins by, as I stated, that Lieutenant Colonel Popovic asked to be connected with General Krstic, and he was not there, so he then asked to be connected with the OC. What is the OC in the context of someone calling the Drina Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can talk about this not only in this particular context but in general [as interpreted]. This refers to the operations centre where the duty operations officer usually sits.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know someone that may have been on duty in the operations centre on 16 July named Rasic, with the nickname Rale?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, at the Drina Corps we did not have an officer by the surname of Rasic, especially not within the Command of the Drina Corps. I don't think that any of the officers with the surname of Rasic would be there with whom Lieutenant Colonel Popovic would contact concerning the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, line 22, which is still on the screen, I believe that the answer was not interpreted in precise terms. The General actually said, "I cannot speak about this particular context but only in general terms."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Visnjic. I too heard that. Does the Prosecutor have any objections? Is there an answer that needs to be corrected? No? Very well. Thank you. The transcript has been corrected. Thank you very much, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there an operations centre at the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At every command, starting from the brigade or regimental level, there would be an operations centre and a duty operations officer there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But to find you on 16 July, what operations centre would anyone call to find you, who, as you say, were at the forward command post in Krivaca?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular context, I see no reason at all for Lieutenant Colonel Popovic to ask for me. I didn't know where that person was, and, well, if he wanted to look for me, he should have done so through the operations centre of the Drina Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, General, but my question was: If someone was to try to call you at the Krivaca forward command post, let's say from Zvornik, what operations centre would they call?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operations centre of the Drina Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the operations centre, to find you, would patch them down to you at the Krivaca forward command post. Is that how it works?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what the communications people know best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you know it too?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I myself being from the infantry, this is a type of communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mediation in communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when communication comes through Zvornik to the operations centre and gets patched down to the forward command post in Krivaca, those communications are on open lines and interceptable, are they not?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those lines are protected ones.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm afraid we didn't hear the beginning of the answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, they had a hard time hearing you again. Your voice is falling off, so you need to try to speak into the mic if you can.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the protected lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But a communications person may know better than you about these particular lines, would he not? Say --

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in any case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. On page 2 of the English there's a mention of Vidoje Blagojevic, who, as we know now, is the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, and there's talk in this intercept of Blagojevic's men arriving to some event on the 16th associated with Colonel Popovic, late. Do you recall Drazen Erdemovic's testimony that the men from Bratunac arrived in the afternoon to assist them in the executions at Branjevo Farm on July 16th?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He spoke about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's mention of a --

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, Erdemovic did, but I don't know whether these are the soldiers in question. I'm not familiar with the fact that they were detached [as interpreted] and under whose orders, except for what I heard during the trial and on the basis of documents, and yesterday during your examination, that as of the 14th, one or two companies of the Zvornik Brigade had to be dispatched for the purposes of reinforcement, for combat operations with the forces of the 2nd Corps of the BH army, and the 28th Division of the BH army as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By my interpretation, you said, "One or two companies of the Zvornik Brigade had to be dispatched." Did you mean Bratunac Brigade or Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the report of Colonel Milanovic and Colonel Blagojevic, the report of the 14th or the 15th, I don't think -- I don't know exactly the date -- that somebody ordered that one to two companies should be sent to the Zvornik Brigade for the purposes of reinforcing the troops of the Zvornik Brigade in combat operations along the front lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but those were Bratunac Brigade troops that were sent up to Zvornik, is that right, not Zvornik Brigade troops?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit 650A.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. I am referring -- I'm talking about this in the context of the previous documents, the documents that we have already discussed, not in the context of this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, if the General could be given the B/C/S version of this. And I know it's a little difficult to make out. This is another familiar intercept from 17 July at 0615 hours. And by the note at the top, it is between General Krstic and Captain Trbic, and then switchboard and then Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, General, is there a Captain Trbic in Zvornik, that you know?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that there was a person by that surname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't there a Captain Trbic that worked in the security branch under Drago Nikolic, Chief of Zvornik Security?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not familiar with that at all. I didn't even know who the chief of Zvornik security was until this trial; in particular, the fact that a Captain Trbic would have been with that particular service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if we read the first couple of lines, it starts off with T saying, "Yes," and then K: "General Krstic." And then T says, "Go ahead, General, sir. This is duty operations officer, Captain Trbic." And then Krstic says, "Trbic!" And then T says, "Yes. Go ahead." And then Krstic says, "What's new?" At 0615 hours on 17 July are you already up and about?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not involved in this conversation at all. I didn't take part in it. There's no -- security chiefs are never on duty within an operations service. They have their own duty service. This is something that is regulated with the military rules.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that's --

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, Mr. McCloskey. -- if this Captain Trbic was at all with the Security Service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I understand that's your general response to these intercepts. I would like to ask you just specific questions related to their substance or their names on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But I see, Your Honour, that it's break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is indeed. We will have a 15-minute break at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Krstic, I'll read a bit more of this and then ask you about some of the information in it, and after it said Trbic, "T" says, "Yes? Go ahead." And "K" says, "What's new?" And "T" says, "Well, everything is under control so far. There are no problems to yesterday's report." Now, you have seen the interim daily combat report of July 16th from Vinko Pandurevic where he describes the combat situation that occurred between the column and 2nd Corps where all the Serb casualties occurred. Did you receive that interim combat report of 16 July from Vinko Pandurevic describing the situation that I've just described?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I have the exhibit, please, the interim combat report of the 16th?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, we can get that for you, but the question is: Did you receive that -- if you need to read the report. Did you receive any interim combat reports down in Krivaca on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Bratunac Brigade and Colonel Milanovic. Apart from that, I didn't receive any interim combat reports, apart from the ones from the Bratunac Brigade and Colonel Milanovic. Maybe that was dispatched to the Command of the Drina Corps. That is why I would like to have a look at the exhibit, and I should like to ask if I may be shown the exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'll withdraw the questions regarding that, because I don't have it on hand right now, but we'll try to bring that back. So on the 16th of July, many Muslim soldiers were killed in the Zvornik Brigade area of responsibility, were they not?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learnt of that during the proceedings here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could provide the General Exhibit 614A. It is the interim combat report of 16 July. The B/C/S version there. And if you could put the English version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, could you clarify your question when you said on the 16th of July, many Muslim soldiers were killed in the Zvornik Brigade area of responsibility. You mean killed in battle or murdered?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I mean killed in battle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can ignore the highlighted remarks or the highlighted parts. I think that's just our internal ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could move the -- yeah. Move it up some more so we can get the full context of the English report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is the submission of the Prosecution, General, that in this intercept, the question, "Okay. Have you killed the Turks up there?" was reference to the Muslim column that were killed during battle and that the report in question is this report before you, which makes reference to having several hundred Muslims killed in a combat operation on 16 July. And I note in the intercept, "T" says, "Well, I guess you got the report. What more can I tell you?" And "K" says, "I got it." And, again, this is Exhibit 650A. So now that you've had a chance to review this, did you receive this particular interim combat report, 650A?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned this exhibit and this conversation. This is -- I never had this conversation with Trbic, neither did I ever get this interim combat report because it was not sent to the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is it your understanding that the column was broken up during this combat that occurred on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this report you mean? Do you mean this report?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of your knowledge, getting it from anything, this report, this court, your experience, your participation.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no previous knowledge about that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go down towards the bottom of the page of the Exhibit 650A, the intercept, where according to the intercept there's a conversation now between Krstic -- General Krstic and Vinko, and makes a reference that the Vinko is a commander. The Commander of the Zvornik Brigade is named Vinko Pandurevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'll read the relevant passage. "K: This is Krstic. P: Hello, General, sir. K: Hello, Vinko. Vinko! P: Go ahead. K: Are there any changes in reference to that report? P: Nothing significant. Basically, we'll probably finish this today. K: Finish it? P: Yes. K: Good. P: We'll go up there today to comb it and consolidate and the defence line will practically be where it used to be. There is a stretch about 300-400 metres long that's open. Those three trenches of ours. We are parallel to them and so far there have been no problems." Did you have this conversation with Vinko Pandurevic on this date, 17 July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that I never had this conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the position of the front lines didn't change very much after the major battle that occurred on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about these problems at all, except for what Colonel Cerovic, on the 20th of July, told me at the forward command post of Godjinje [phoen], but I had no other information than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get information about the front lines and the positioning of the front lines in Zvornik after this combat?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I have already said, this report was not sent to the forward command post but to the command of the Drina Corps. It never reached the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you concerned, after a major battle, whether or not the front line had changed at all at this time, July 17th? Wouldn't that be something you would be concerned about no matter what your position?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably it would. If the situation were such, of the type that you have described, then somebody would order the offensive to be stopped towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Cerovic tell you about?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said -- briefly, he informed me about that area of responsibility of the corps on the 20th. He said that there were a lot of problems, considerable problems, in the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade, and that an offensive had been launched from the Tuzla direction by the forces of the 2nd Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the 28th Division, from the rear. He also told me that the situation had been normalised on the 20th, when he informed me of that, and he also told me that pursuant to orders of the Main Staff, we should set aside a portion of the units and send them to the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps, to deploy them there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting, Mr. McCloskey, but I have a question. General Krstic, you said that Cerovic, I think, informed you that there had been quite a number of problems. Did he specify? Did he mention the type of problems that were being encountered? What type of problems?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing special. He just said that they were having problems and that the situation in the area of responsibility of Zvornik and the 1st Birac Brigade had been brought back to normal. He said that the situation had been normalised. That's how he described it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you have the curiosity -- were you curious to know what type of problems they had been having?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he described the situation in the way he did, I didn't ask him anything special, because the Zepa operation was ongoing and I had to continue with the implementation of my assignments in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but as commander, are you convinced that one can learn by the problems one is having to avoid them in future, avoid having the same problems in future?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't speak about any special problems except for the ones he mentioned, and quite simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, General, but the question is, and I'm going to repeat the question: He said that he was having considerable problems, but were you not interested in knowing what those problems actually were, what his problems were? Were you curious to know?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All he said was that there were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Very well. I'm not going to insist. Mr. McCloskey, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I have one question. General, to your knowledge, was General Zivanovic at the regular command post in Vlasenica most of the week from the 13th through the 17th, or did he, to your knowledge, come and go? Did he show up there every day, or do you know whether he was there most of the time, in Vlasenica, at the command post, General Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Zivanovic was the commander of the corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had the right to choose where he would be. So I myself don't know where he was at the time, whether he was at the command post at Vlasenica all the time or some other spot in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was up to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand that. My next question is: What would the usual army procedure be if a communique or a report comes to the command post and the commander is not there? What would the procedure be? Let it just stay until he comes? Would it go to the next in command, which, under your argument, was yourself, who was still the deputy commander and Chief of Staff, or would it be sent on to him wherever he was? What would happen to a report that came to the command post if the commander was not there?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At all events, these reports and communiques had to reach the commander, and I was involved in my assignment towards Zepa. I was busy with that. And it is quite understandable that they would not have informed me about that except for the Corps Commander who was there. He would be informed and he would take steps, whether he was at the command post or somewhere around in the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade, Milici Brigade, Zvornik Brigade, or whatever, Birac Brigade or Vlasenica Brigade. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So your answer, if I understand it, is that whoever the commander was, if he wasn't at the command post when a report or a communique of some importance came, whoever was on duty would take steps to get it to him, wherever he was; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If it was urgent, it would be dispatched immediately. If it wasn't that urgent, then it could wait for the commander's return and then be handed to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, you said that it was quite understandable that the reports or communiques did not reach the forward command post, but was it understandable that no information reached you with respect to the situation that was evolving? When you said "understandable," I'm using your own words. I'm using the term "understandable."

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. It was understandable if the Corps Commander was there and present and following and monitoring the situation, and the Corps Commander knew full well where I was, where I was engaged, and what problems I was facing with respect to my assignment for Zepa. So it was not logical to burden me with that if he himself was there, because we were able to pull out a portion of the Zvornik Brigade and, pursuant to orders from the Corps Commander, return them back to the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade. Therefore, the Zvornik Brigade no longer existed towards Zepa. All its forces were down there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, General. I was speaking about understandability with respect to reports and communiques. You said that it was understandable. Now, I insisted upon the fact that was it understandable that no information reached you? You said that that was understandable. It didn't reach you, the commander, at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll repeat what I said. There was -- the Zvornik Brigade was not there any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, General. Never mind. I'm not going to repeat my question. Please continue, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Krstic, on the 17th of July in the Zepa operation, would you have liked to have had Vinko Pandurevic back assisting you in that operation?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Why? I had enough troops for the operation towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Vinko Pandurevic and his unit were part of the original troops that were sent down there, and they, as we know, had to be pulled back right as the operation was going. So are you saying today you didn't need him back at all?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not pulled out in the midst of the operation but at the very beginning of the operation. And aside from the pullout of that part of the Zvornik Brigade -- I mean, apart from them. I had enough forces for the purposes of my operation towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit 652A. And this is a 17 July intercept between Bedem, Krstic, and the name Veletic is mentioned but cannot be heard, according to this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Krstic, what is the code name Bedem?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware of a Colonel Veletic that was part of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Veletic was Chief of Artillery with the Drina Corps, if that indeed is the same person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's another Colonel Veletic, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a very common surname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had a unit in the Drina Corps called the 4th Drinski Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a temporary formation which was not part of the overall structure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Colonel Veletic in command of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. He may have been. As I said, it was a temporary formation which was -- which would be established if necessary. That was the unit that I found when I came back from my treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the same Colonel Veletic that you mentioned was the Chief of Artillery, Colonel Stojan Veletic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Colonel Stojan Veletic is Chief of Artillery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have a communication -- excuse me. Did you ever want Lieutenant Colonel Vlacic to return to his unit?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know anything about the fact that Lieutenant Colonel Vlacic was outside of his brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you step to the diagram that we have with the pointer and look over the far side of it. The big exhibit is 28/1. And could you look where we have noted on the far right-hand bottom the 4th Drinski Brigade Commander Colonel Stojan Veletic and the Chief of Staff Lieutenant Colonel Ljubomir Vlacic. Do you see them and can you point those out?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what's written here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that structure correct? Does this help refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Vlacic was the Chief of Staff of the 1st Birac Brigade, and I don't know anything about him being on this post, that is, the Chief of Staff of this temporary brigade, especially in that period of time, that is, at the time a breakthrough was carried out by the 28th Division and an attack launched by the 2nd Corps of the BH army from the direction of Tuzla towards the area where Lieutenant Colonel Vlacic was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could go to the other end of the diagram and you'll see the organigramme for the Birac Brigade, and we see Lieutenant Colonel Vlacic there also. On July 17th, can you tell us -- can you point out on the far left side on the bottom again is the Birac.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Birac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can take a seat. Thank you, General. On 17 July, what was the -- what were the duties of Lieutenant Colonel Vlacic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Vlacic was the Chief of Staff of the 1st Birac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you -- was he working in the Sarajevo-Romanija area with the 4th Drinski Brigade on the 17 July?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to Exhibit 661A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is an intercept of 17 July. It's the date that the mobilisation order was signed by you that we talked about yesterday. And this is a conversation between a general who is at Zlatar, which we know to be the Drina Corps headquarters in Vlasenica. On 17 July, did you order that Colonel Popovic report to the forward command post in Krivaca?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV KRSTIC [Resumed]
